events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.55)
events.body:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI ride, so any unexplained extra distance flows into the fare: distance is billed by the meter and total charged was $36.67 with distance fare $23.84 over 16.91 km [F4][F7][RD-2]. One off-route segment is recorded: 21:26–21:37, 6.64 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.76 km, adding 4.89 km and straying up to 2070 m from the optimal route [F3]; the whole trip ran 16.9 km vs 11.6 km optimal [F1], which under RD-1 is a deviation requiring review segment by segment [RD-1][RD-2].

The only possible excuse on the record is the rider's chat consent. The driver asked at 21:23 whether he could "go round via Balestier Road" and the rider replied at 21:24 "Can lah, go ahead" [F8][F9][F10] — a rider message timestamped before the segment began (21:26), so it satisfies the timing limb of RD-5 [RD-5]. But the consent named a specific road, Balestier Road, and a specific-road agreement covers driving on that road only; the record must tie the segment to that road [RD-5]. Nothing does: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path (the traffic facts name Central Expressway, Bishan Street 11 and Braddell Road, none of which is a placement of the car on Balestier Road) [F12][F13][F14], and the only thing tying the driver's account to Balestier Road is his own post-trip statement [F11], which alone is not consent and cannot establish the driven path [RD-5][G11]. The driver's statement does not place the segment somewhere else either — it repeats Balestier Road — so this is neither "tied" nor "elsewhere"; the record simply cannot settle whether the 4.89 km extra was the agreed Balestier route or an unrelated loop [RD-5]. This finding controls the amount, so I cannot fix a refund figure, and it goes to a human [RD-5][G13].

The driver's separate RD-4 claim of avoiding congestion is not established. The only speed-band evidence covering the detour window is Central Expressway band 2 (10–19 km/h) [F12], and band records alone do not exempt; the qualifying incident limb fails — no incident was recorded near the route [F15][RD-4]. There is also no rider-named stop: the rider named no place, no stop was measured in the segment, and RD-3 therefore does not apply [F8][F9][RD-3]. No prior upheld route dispute exists on either profile, so RD-6 raises no account flag [F17][F18][RD-6]. I read the chat, the driver's statement and the complaint: no threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegations appear, so the safety screen is "none" [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1]. Evidence is otherwise complete (all chat messages timestamped, GPS measurements present) [F10][F3], but the one element my ruling needs — which road the 21:26–21:37 segment actually ran on — is not in the record [RD-5][G13].
